svg.text: FIGURE 1: LUMPED-MATTER ABSTRACTION & TELLEGEN POWER CONSERVATION ENGINE
Physical Foundations, Maxwell to LMA Collapse, Passive Sign Convention, Tellegen Invariance & Non-Superposition

g.text: • Maxwell's field equations collapse to circuit theory when:
λ = c / f ≫ d (d = max circuit dimension)
• Speed of light c ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s; propagation delay Δt → 0.
• Voltages and currents become pure time functions: v(t), i(t).
1. Electric and magnetic fields are strictly confined within elements.
2. Total charge accumulation on any closed lumped element is zero.
3. Magnetic flux linkage ∂B/∂t outside elements is negligible.
4. KCL and KVL hold identically at every instant of time.
Comparison: Field Theory vs. Circuit Theory
• Transmission Lines: When length l ≥ 0.01 λ, wave propagation
and reflection cannot be neglected → distributed parameters!
• High-Frequency Antennas: Radiative loss occurs when fields
are unconfined → circuit abstraction fails completely.
• Changing Magnetic Flux: If ∂B/∂t passes through circuit loop,
• Elementary Charge: e = 1.602176 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (negative for e⁻).
• Number of electrons in 1 Coulomb: n = 1/e ≈ 6.242 × 10¹⁸.
• Charge can neither be created nor destroyed, only transferred.
• Current definition: i(t) = dq(t)/dt (1 Ampere = 1 Coulomb/sec).
• Charge integral: q(t) = q(t₀) + ∫ i(τ) dτ from t₀ to t.
Open-circuit boundary: i_open = 0 A (no charge passage possible).
• Work done per unit charge moving between points A and B:
v = dw / dq (1 Volt = 1 Joule / Coulomb)
• Potential Rise: Moving from (-) to (+) terminal (gain in energy).
• Potential Drop: Moving from (+) to (-) terminal (loss of energy).
• Short-circuit boundary: v_short = 0 V (zero potential difference).
Electric Power & Instantaneous Rate of Energy
• Power is the time rate of expanding or absorbing energy:
w(t) = ∫ p(τ) dτ from t₀ to t = ∫ v(τ) i(τ) dτ
• Commercial energy unit: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ Joules = 3.6 MJ.
• Average Power: P_avg = (1/T) ∫ p(t) dt over one complete period T.
DC vs. AC vs. Impulse Waveform Taxonomy
★ Crest Factor CF = I_peak / I_rms | Form Factor FF = I_rms / I_avg
• Ideal Voltage Source: Maintains v(t) = V_s REGARDLESS of load current.
• Practical Voltage Source: Terminal voltage drops with load current:
V_L = V_s - I_L · R_s (R_s in SERIES)
• Ideal Current Source: Supplies i(t) = I_s REGARDLESS of load voltage.
• Practical Current Source: Delivered current decreases with load voltage:
I_L = I_s - V_L / R_s (R_s in PARALLEL)
Case A: Absorbing Power (Load / Passive Mode)
• Reference current enters the POSITIVE reference terminal:
• If P_abs > 0: Element truly consumes / dissipates energy.
• If P_abs < 0: Element is actually DELIVERING energy!
Case B: Delivering Power (Source / Active Mode)
• Reference current leaves the POSITIVE reference terminal:
Exam Trap Drill: Power In Dependent Branches
Circuit: 10 V source in series with 2 Ω resistor and dependent source 2 I_x.
I_x is current flowing through the loop from source to dependent source.
Step 3: Check Current Direction w.r.t Dependent Source:
• Current I_x = 2.5 A enters the POSITIVE terminal of dependent source!
• 10 V Source: P_del = (10 V) · (2.5 A) = 25.0 W delivered.
• 2 Ω Resistor: P_abs = I_x² · R = (2.5)² · 2 = 12.5 W absorbed.
★ Fatal Error: Dependent sources are NOT always active generators; they can absorb power!
• For ANY lumped network with b branches satisfying KCL and KVL:
• Mathematical Origin: Orthogonality of KCL cutset space and KVL loop space:
v_b^T · i_b = (B_f^T · v_l)^T · i_b = v_l^T · (B_f · i_b) = v_l^T · 0 = 0
Independent of element nature! Valid for linear, non-linear, time-varying, active.
• If two networks N and N' have identical graph topology but
different element values, source excitations, or operating frequencies:
1. Proof of Reciprocity Theorem in passive bilateral networks.
2. Adjoint Network sensitivity calculations in analog CAD simulators.
3. Bounds on impedance and driving-point functions.
★ DANGER: Power Superposition is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN!
• Superposition applies ONLY to linear functions (L[ax + by] = aL[x] + bL[y]).
• Electric power is quadratic: P = i²R = v²/R (strictly non-linear!).
i_total = i₁ ± i₂ ⇒ P_total = (i₁ ± i₂)² R
P_total = i₁²R + i₂²R ± 2 i₁ i₂ R = P₁ + P₂ ± 2 √(P₁ P₂)
Example: P₁ = 9 W, P₂ = 4 W ⇒ P_max = (3+2)² = 25 W; P_min = (3-2)² = 1 W!
The ONLY Exception: Orthogonal Harmonic Signals
• If sources operate at DIFFERENT harmonic frequencies or DC + AC:
i(t) = I_DC + I_m1 sin(ω₁ t) + I_m2 sin(ω₂ t)
• The cross-product terms vanish over fundamental period T:
∫ sin(ω₁ t) · sin(ω₂ t) dt = 0 (for ω₁ ≠ ω₂)
• In that orthogonal regime, average power DOES add up:
P_avg = P_DC + P_AC1 + P_AC2 = [I_DC² + I_rms1² + I_rms2²] R
★ Golden Rule: Power superposition is valid IF AND ONLY IF frequencies are distinct!
